Which of the following famines was the worst in the southern country?
x:
The Guntur Famine of 1833, popularly known as the Dokkala Karuvu, is regarded as one of the most devastating famines in the history of South India. The famine was caused by the failure of monsoons, severe drought and inadequate colonial relief measures. Agricultural production collapsed, leading to acute food shortages, starvation and widespread loss of life. Contemporary records describe large- scale migration, disease and mortality during this period. The famine exposed the weaknesses of the British revenue administration, which continued to collect land revenue despite widespread crop failure. The tragedy later influenced discussions on irrigation development, eventually leading to major irrigation projects under engineers such as Sir Arthur Cotton.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (4).

s: Who was the Andhra official who helped Sir Arthur Cotton in the construction of the Godavari Dam?
x:
Veenam Veeranna was an eminent Andhra engineer and administrator who rendered valuable assistance to Sir Arthur Cotton during the construction of the Dowleswaram (Godavari) Anicut. His knowledge of local conditions, irrigation practices and river behaviour greatly contributed to the successful execution of the project. The Godavari Anicut transformed the Godavari delta into one of the most fertile agricultural regions in India and is regarded as one of the greatest irrigation achievements of the 19th century.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (2).

s: In which year was the Dhavaleswaram Dam constructed?
x:
The Dowleswaram (Dhavaleswaram) Anicut across the Godavari River was completed in 1855 under the supervision of Sir Arthur Cotton. The anicut transformed the Godavari delta into one of India's most fertile agricultural regions by providing assured irrigation. Sir Arthur Cotton is therefore remembered as the "Architect of Modern Andhra Agriculture."
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (3).
